parts.note: Brookner's 1988 novel takes its plural title from people who arrive after the expected time

clue.text: His best-known works neatly concluded by Marlowe

parts.note: the author's famous novels are wrapped up by his detective Philip Marlowe, not by the Elizabethan playwright of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Marlowe first suggests Christopher Marlowe the dramatist; here it is the private eye whose cases end the American author's books.
explanation.definitionFit: The American crime writer created Philip Marlowe, who solves the cases in his best-known novels.

parts.note: the French saying attributed to Flaubert puts God in the small particulars of a work

unwell means ill

explanation.definitionFit: Drusilla is the name of Roman imperial women, such as Livia Drusilla, wife of Augustus and first empress.

clue.text: Rue meal badly cooked for a cousin of Richard II

indicators.note: badly cooked suggests the ingredients rue and meal are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a poorly prepared dinner served to a royal relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of this title, son of York, is Richard II's cousin and loyal supporter in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Outstanding features of work by Lucas

definitions.meaning: prominent sights or turning points that stand out
a book of that title by the essayist E. V. Lucas

explanation.definitionFit: Prominent objects in a landscape that stand out are the word's everyday sense; it is also a Lucas title.

parts.note: Lessing's heroine has the surname Quest, a synonym of search, in the Children of Violence novels

clue.text: Stephen Dedalus when first portrayed

parts.note: Joyce first portrayed Stephen in A Portrait of the Artist as a ..., the last two words of the title

clue.text: Puzzle out crime for victim of Verona vendetta

explanation.surface: A detective must solve a crime to find who was killed in an Italian feud.

clue.text: Dennis book rock solid

clue.text: Mercy Warren's French admirer

parts.note: Mercy Otis Warren's 1772 satirical play has a French-spelt title meaning a flatterer

clue.text: Reportedly very young poet taking cavalier decisions

clue.text: Creator of John Clayton said to be capable of producing a rabbit

clue.text: Withdrawal by Reid

clue.text: Journey by Forster

parts.note: E. M. Forster's second novel is The ... Journey, missing its adjective

explanation.definitionFit: Forster's 1907 novel is The Longest Journey, so the word completes the title.

clue.text: Dagger found in Macbeth's robe, lustrously ornamented!

explanation.surface: Macbeth's dagger is discovered inside his gleaming, ornate robe.

explanation.definitionFit: A dagger in printing is the obelisk mark, also called by this Greek-derived name.

clue.text: An alarm from Hammond Innes

clue.text: Some insincere smile greeted slave driver

clue.text: Ordinary seaman revealing general opinion of television drama
